title: Game of Life: when does test-time recursion still generalize?
hypothesis: A weight-tied recurrent cell trained to roll out Game of Life to depth 3 will extrapolate to deeper rollouts better than an untied per-step stack; a capacity sweep reveals where.
question: When does weight-tying buy test-time recursion depth-generalization?
method: Tiny conv cell applied recurrently (tied) vs a per-step stack (untied); sweep hidden width H in {1,2,4,24}; train rollout depth 3, evaluate depth 6.

metrics.headline: at H=4 the tied cell extrapolates perfectly (1.0) while the untied 3x-param stack decays (0.61)

result_summary: Capacity window: at H=4 tied recursion learns the exact reusable rule and extrapolates to unseen depths (1.0) while untied (3x params) fails (0.61); H=2 tied is unstable; H=24 both perfect.

title: Superposition phase diagram: does feature correlation resist or reshape superposition?
hypothesis: Raising within-pair activation correlation pushes paired features toward local orthogonality and delays superposition onset, because co-occurring features pay interference cost on every sample.
question: Across a (density x correlation) grid, do correlated feature pairs orthogonalize or merge, and how does the superposition phase boundary move?
method: Anthropic-style toy autoencoder ReLU(W^T W x + b), n=16 features in 8 pairs -> m=4 dims; within-pair indicator correlation exactly rho via shared-coin mixture; sweep p in {0.02..0.9} x rho in {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}, 2 seeds, 3000 online Adam steps.
architecture: linear encoder/decoder tied W (4x16) + bias, ReLU output (~68 params)

metrics.headline: correlated pairs MERGE (within-pair |cos| 0.34->0.97 at p=0.05) instead of orthogonalizing, and correlation extends superposition into the dense regime (1.0 -> 2.25 feats/dim at p=0.9)

result_summary: Hypothesis refuted: across the grid, raising within-pair correlation makes the model collapse each pair onto one shared direction (within-pair |cos| ~ 1.0 for rho>=0.5, p>=0.1) rather than forming local orthogonal bases; merging halves the effective feature count, so superposition persists into densities where uncorrelated features collapse to one-feature-per-dim.
